docs.title: nowcastgermany
docs.text:
The German COVID-19 hospitalisation nowcasting hub as a case study: its reporting triangle as forecast tasks, the benchmark and its page.

nowcastgermany is the package in packages/nowcastgermany of the repository (Packages).

docs.title: Install
docs.text: uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/nowcastgermany"

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The hub's reporting triangle gives each Meldedatum's count as first reported (value_0d) and the change reported on each later day. We make a small one for two states, Germany as their sum, and two of Germany's age groups.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
days = pd.date_range("2021-09-01", "2021-11-28").date.astype(str)
changes = ["value_0d", "value_1d", "value_2d"]
rows = []
for state, size in (("DE-BY", 40), ("DE-BE", 20)):
    trend = size * np.exp(np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.1, len(days))))
    for day, mean in zip(days, trend):
        counts = rng.poisson((mean / 2, mean / 4, mean / 4))
        rows.append((day, state, "00+", *counts, 0))
wide = pd.DataFrame(
    rows, columns=["date", "location", "age_group", *changes, "value_>80d"]
)
germany = wide.groupby("date", as_index=False).sum(numeric_only=True)
germany = germany.assign(location="DE", age_group="00+")
ages = [
    germany.assign(age_group=age, **{c: germany[c] // 2 for c in changes})
    for age in ("35-59", "60-79")
]
wide = pd.concat([wide, germany, *ages], ignore_index=True)[wide.columns]
wide.to_csv("COVID-19_hospitalizations.csv", index=False)

hub_triangle reads it as one row per Meldedatum, place and report date, with the count reported by then.

from nowcastgermany.data import hub_triangle

triangle = hub_triangle("COVID-19_hospitalizations.csv")
assert list(triangle.columns) == [
    "reference_date",
    "location",
    "age_group",
    "confirm",
    "report_date",
]

nowcast_tasks makes the two tasks of a nowcast date: Germany with its states, and Germany with its age groups. Their target dates are the ends of the hub's 7-day sums, from the nowcast date to 28 days before it.

from nowcastgermany.data import nowcast_tasks

states, age_groups = nowcast_tasks(
    triangle, "2021-11-21", n_samples=100, seed=1
)
assert states.locations == ("CD-BE", "CD-BY")
assert age_groups.locations == ("CD-A3", "CD-A4")
assert len(states.target_end_dates) == 29

docs.title: Name the hub's places
docs.text:
The tasks code Germany as the country CD, its states as provinces and its age groups as CD-A<i>. level gives the level each place is scored at.

from nowcastgermany.data import level, place_code

assert place_code("DE") == "CD"
assert place_code("DE-BY") == "CD-BY"
assert place_code("DE", "35-59") == "CD-A3"
levels = [level(p) for p in ("DE", "DE-BY", "35-59")]
assert levels == ["national", "states", "age"]

docs.title: Score models on the benchmark
docs.text:
germany_forecasts runs registered models on each nowcast date and keeps their quantiles at the hub's levels. Here the two baselines nowcast the last three 7-day sums.

from nowcastgermany.evaluation import germany_forecasts

forecasts = germany_forecasts(
    ["randomwalk", "randomwalknowcast"],
    triangle,
    ["2021-11-21"],
    n_samples=100,
    seed=1,
    horizons=(0, -1, -2),
)
places = {"DE", "DE-BE", "DE-BY", "35-59", "60-79"}
assert set(forecasts["location"]) == places

with_truth adds each sum's truth, its count reported $D$ days after it ends. score_germany scores the forecasts by WIS and interval coverage, as the hub did. relative_scores divides each model's scores by a reference model's, on the forecasts both made.

from nowcastgermany.evaluation import relative_scores, score_germany, with_truth

scores = score_germany(with_truth(forecasts, triangle, 5), 5)
assert set(scores["pool"]) == {"national", "states", "age"}
skill = relative_scores(scores, ["target"], "randomwalknowcast")
reference = skill.loc[skill["model"] == "randomwalknowcast"]
assert reference["rel_wis"].iloc[0] == 1.0

docs.title: Keep the held-out half out of the page
docs.text:
The nowcast dates are split at a split date, and the later half is held out for the paper. held_out_leaks lists any held-out date the page's files name.

from pathlib import Path

from nowcastgermany.reporting import held_out_leaks

Path("summary.json").write_text('{"last": "2021-12-01"}')
assert held_out_leaks([Path("summary.json")], "2022-01-01") == []
assert held_out_leaks([Path("summary.json")], "2021-11-29") != []

docs.title: nowcastgermany.data
docs.text:
The German COVID-19 hospitalisation nowcasting hub data as forecast tasks.

The German hub (Wolffram et al. 2023) collected nowcasts of the 7-day hospitalisation incidence by Meldedatum, the date a case was reported positive, for Germany, its 16 federal states and six age groups. Its reporting triangle gives each Meldedatum's count as first reported, the change reported on each of the next 80 days, and the changes after that in one column. hub_triangle turns it into one row per Meldedatum, place and report date with the count reported by then, the layout of epinowcast's germany_covid19_hosp, which read_triangle reads.

nowcast_tasks makes the tasks of one nowcast date in the ForecastTask form, so every registered model runs on them unchanged.

  • Each report date up to the nowcast date is a release with that date as its cut-off, and the Meldedatum is the onset date.
  • Germany is the country. The states are provinces in one task and the age groups provinces in another, each summing to Germany (place_code).
  • The hub's targets are the 7-day sums ending on every day from the nowcast date to 28 days before it, and the days after it to forecast (HORIZONS). A nowcast date gives one pair of tasks whose target dates are all of them, so every sum comes from one forecast with one context end. Dates are real: the nowcast date is the cut-off, whatever its weekday, and every model forecasts every target date.

hub_forecasts moves the forecasts back and names the places as the hub does, and hub_target gives the 7-day sums as each report date gives them, the truth they are scored on.

def place_code(location: str, age_group: str = ALL_AGES) -> str:
    """Return the location code a hub place has in the tasks.

    Parameters
    ----------
    location : str
        The hub's location, `DE` or a state such as `DE-BY`.
    age_group : str
        The hub's age group. Only Germany has age groups other than
        `ALL_AGES`.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        `CD` for Germany, `CD-<state>` for a state and `CD-A<i>` for the
        i-th of `AGE_GROUPS`.
    """
    if age_group != ALL_AGES:
        return f"{NATIONAL}-A{AGE_GROUPS.index(age_group)}"
    if location == GERMANY:
        return NATIONAL
    return f"{NATIONAL}-{location.removeprefix(f'{GERMANY}-')}"

def level(place: str) -> str:
    """Return the paper's level of a place.

    Parameters
    ----------
    place : str
        A place in `PLACE_NAMES`.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        `national` for Germany, `age` for an age group and `states` for a
        state.
    """
    if place == GERMANY:
        return "national"
    return "age" if place in AGE_GROUPS else "states"

def hub_changes(wide: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the hub's wide triangle as one change per reported delay.

    The changes after 80 days are at 81 days, as epinowcast's
    `germany_covid19_hosp` puts them. A missing change is a report date
    after the file was made, so it has no row.

    Parameters
    ----------
    wide : pandas.DataFrame
        The hub's `COVID-19_hospitalizations.csv`: columns `date`,
        `location`, `age_group`, `value_0d` to `value_80d` and
        `value_>80d`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `date`, `location`, `age_group`, `delay` (days) and `change`.
    """
    changes = [c for c in wide.columns if c.startswith("value_")]
    long = wide.melt(
        id_vars=["date", "location", "age_group"],
        value_vars=changes,
        var_name="delay",
        value_name="change",
    ).dropna(subset=["change"])
    long["delay"] = long["delay"].map({c: i for i, c in enumerate(changes)})
    return long

def hub_triangle(path: Path | str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read the hub's reporting triangle as counts by report date.

    The changes, cumulated, of `hub_changes`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        The hub's `COVID-19_hospitalizations.csv`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        As `read_triangle`.
    """
    long = hub_changes(pd.read_csv(path)).sort_values(
        ["location", "age_group", "date", "delay"]
    )
    long["confirm"] = (
        long.groupby(["location", "age_group", "date"])["change"]
        .cumsum()
        .astype("int64")
    )
    report = pd.to_datetime(long["date"]) + pd.to_timedelta(
        long["delay"], unit="D"
    )
    out = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "reference_date": long["date"],
            "location": long["location"],
            "age_group": long["age_group"],
            "confirm": long["confirm"],
            "report_date": report.dt.date.astype(str),
        }
    )
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def within_delay(triangle: pd.DataFrame, days: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the counts reported at most `days` days after their Meldedatum.

    A count's latest row is then its count `days` days on: the 40-day
    truth's count of a sum's last day
    (`packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml`, `[truth]`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        As `read_triangle`.
    days : int
        The longest delay kept, in days.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The rows of `triangle` reported within `days` days.
    """
    delay = pd.to_datetime(triangle["report_date"]) - pd.to_datetime(
        triangle["reference_date"]
    )
    return triangle.loc[delay <= pd.Timedelta(days=days)].reset_index(drop=True)

def nowcast_tasks(
    triangle: pd.DataFrame,
    nowcast_date: str,
    n_samples: int,
    seed: int,
    horizons: Sequence[int] = HORIZONS,
) -> list[ForecastTask]:
    """Return the states and the age groups task of a nowcast date.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        Counts by Meldedatum and report date (`read_triangle`).
    nowcast_date : str
        The nowcast date, ISO format. Report dates after it are left out.
    n_samples : int
        Samples per forecast.
    seed : int
        Seed of the tasks' random numbers.
    horizons : sequence of int
        Days from the nowcast date to the end of each 7-day sum, the
        hub's (`HORIZONS`) by default. Days after it are forecasts.

    Returns
    -------
    list of ForecastTask
        The task of the states in the triangle, then that of the age
        groups, each with Germany as the country. The reference date and
        cut-off are the nowcast date, and the target dates are every
        horizon's day, so one forecast gives every 7-day sum.
    """
    # The hub has age groups for every state, but only Germany's are
    # nowcast.
    rows = triangle.loc[
        (triangle["report_date"] <= nowcast_date)
        & (
            (triangle["age_group"] == ALL_AGES)
            | (triangle["location"] == GERMANY)
        )
    ]
    rows = _carried(rows)
    rows = rows.loc[rows["confirm"] != 0]
    ref = as_date(nowcast_date)
    vintage = rows["report_date"]
    daily = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "vintage": vintage,
            "location": _place_codes(rows["location"], rows["age_group"]),
            "onset_date": rows["reference_date"],
            "observed": rows["confirm"],
            "imputed": 0,
            "cutoff": vintage,
        }
    )[_DAILY]
    weekly = _weekly(daily)
    present = set(daily["location"].unique())
    groups = (
        tuple(place_code(s) for s in STATES if place_code(s) in present),
        tuple(
            place_code(GERMANY, a)
            for a in AGE_GROUPS
            if place_code(GERMANY, a) in present
        ),
    )
    days = tuple(
        (ref + dt.timedelta(days=h)).isoformat() for h in sorted(horizons)
    )
    tasks = []
    for places in groups:
        keep = {NATIONAL, *places}
        own = daily.loc[daily["location"].isin(keep)].reset_index(drop=True)
        history = weekly.loc[weekly["location"].isin(keep)]
        tasks.append(
            ForecastTask(
                vintage=ref.isoformat(),
                reference_date=ref,
                kind="real",
                cutoff=ref.isoformat(),
                target=history.loc[
                    history["vintage"] == ref.isoformat()
                ].reset_index(drop=True),
                delays=None,
                locations=places,
                target_end_dates=days,
                n_samples=n_samples,
                seed=seed,
                target_history=history.reset_index(drop=True),
                daily_history=own,
            )
        )
    return tasks

def hub_forecasts(
    samples: pd.DataFrame, task: ForecastTask, nowcast_date: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one task's forecasts on the hub's dates and places.

    Germany is taken from the states task, as the sum of the states, and
    left out of the age groups task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        `run_forecasts` output for `task` alone.
    task : ForecastTask
        A task of `nowcast_tasks`.
    nowcast_date : str
        Its nowcast date.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model`, `location` (the place, as in `PLACE_NAMES`),
        `forecast_date`, `target_end_date`, `horizon` (days, as
        `HORIZONS`), `sample` and `value`.
    """
    ages = any(_place(c) in AGE_GROUPS for c in task.locations)
    rows = samples.loc[samples["as_of"].isna()]
    if ages:
        rows = rows.loc[rows["location"] != NATIONAL]
    end = pd.to_datetime(rows["target_end_date"])
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "model": rows["model"].to_numpy(),
            "location": [_place(c) for c in rows["location"]],
            "forecast_date": nowcast_date,
            "target_end_date": end.dt.date.astype(str).to_numpy(),
            "horizon": (end - pd.Timestamp(nowcast_date)).dt.days.to_numpy(),
            "sample": rows["sample"].to_numpy(),
            "value": rows["value"].to_numpy(),
        }
    )

def hub_target(triangle: pd.DataFrame, ends: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return 7-day sums as each report date gives them, as a target table.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        Counts by Meldedatum and report date (`read_triangle`).
    ends : sequence of str
        Last days of the 7-day sums.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per place in `PLACE_NAMES`, end and report date from the
        end on: `kind` (`real`), `vintage` and `cutoff` (the report date),
        `location` (the place), `target_end_date` (the end) and `total`.
    """
    places = triangle["location"].where(
        triangle["age_group"] == ALL_AGES, triangle["age_group"]
    )
    keep = places.isin(set(PLACE_NAMES)) & (
        (triangle["age_group"] == ALL_AGES) | (triangle["location"] == GERMANY)
    )
    first = (as_date(min(ends)) - dt.timedelta(days=6)).isoformat()
    rows = triangle.loc[keep & (triangle["reference_date"] >= first)]
    reports = sorted(set(rows["report_date"]) | set(ends))
    days = pd.date_range(first, max(ends), freq="D").date.astype(str)
    frames = []
    for place, own in rows.groupby(places.loc[rows.index]):
        # Count of each Meldedatum (row) by each report date (column).
        counts = (
            own.pivot_table(
                index="reference_date",
                columns="report_date",
                values="confirm",
                aggfunc="last",
            )
            .reindex(index=days, columns=reports)
            .ffill(axis=1)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
        sums = counts.rolling(7).sum()
        for end in ends:
            total = sums.loc[end]
            total = total.loc[total.index >= end]
            frames.append(
                pd.DataFrame(
                    {
                        "kind": "real",
                        "vintage": total.index,
                        "cutoff": total.index,
                        "location": place,
                        "target_end_date": end,
                        "total": total.to_numpy(),
                    }
                )
            )
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

docs.text:
Score our models and the hub teams on the German nowcast benchmark.

The benchmark is that of Wolffram et al. (2023): nowcasts of the 7-day hospitalisation incidence by Meldedatum in Germany, made each day from 2021-11-22 to 2022-04-29, for Germany, its states and its age groups. The hub collected them as quantiles at QUANTILE_LEVELS and scored them by WIS and the coverage of the 50% and 95% intervals. They are scored the same way here.

The nowcast dates are split in two halves at GermanyConfig.split_date. The first half is for developing and checking our setup; the second is held out for the paper (nowcast_dates).

germany_forecasts runs our models on the tasks of each nowcast date (nowcastgermany.data.nowcast_tasks), for the sums ending on every day from 0 to 28 days back (HORIZONS, one task pair per date, so one forecast with one context end gives every sum), and keeps their quantiles at QUANTILE_LEVELS: a model's own where it gives them, else those of its samples (nowcasteval.marginals.forecast_quantiles). team_forecasts takes the hub teams' submitted quantiles at the same horizons. with_truth adds each sum's truth, its count in the data $D$ days after it ends, the paper's 40-day truth (rolling_truth). score_germany scores both by score_quantiles, and relative_scores gives each model's pairwise relative skill, scaled to a reference: randomwalknowcast on the page, the hub's own baseline in the paper. paper_forecasts writes the forecasts as the paper's long table.

def run_models(config: GermanyConfig, held_out: bool) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return the models a half runs: `held_out_models` join the held-out.

    A held-out model that is not registered yet, such as one whose
    checkpoint is still pending, is left out with a warning.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : GermanyConfig
        The settings.
    held_out : bool
        The held-out half rather than the development half.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str
    """
    if not held_out:
        return config.models
    known = {s.name for s in list_models()}
    waiting = [m for m in config.held_out_models if m not in known]
    if waiting:
        log.warning(
            "Held-out models not registered yet, left out: %s.",
            ", ".join(waiting),
        )
    extra = tuple(m for m in config.held_out_models if m in known)
    return (*config.models, *extra)

def nowcast_dates(config: GermanyConfig, held_out: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """Return the nowcast dates of one half, oldest first.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : GermanyConfig

        The held-out half, from the split date on, rather than the
        development half before it.

    -------
    list of str
        ISO dates.
    """
    days = pd.date_range(config.first_date, config.last_date, freq="D")
    dates = [d.date().isoformat() for d in days]
    return [d for d in dates if (d >= config.split_date) == held_out]

def fetch_germany(  # pragma: no cover - network
    config: GermanyConfig, dest: Path | str
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Download the triangle and the teams' submissions at their commits.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : GermanyConfig
        The sources.
    dest : pathlib.Path or str
        Directory the files go to, by base name, with `sources.json`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The sources, also written to `dest/sources.json`.
    """
    out = Path(dest)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = [(config.repo, config.commit, config.triangle)] + [
        (config.teams_repo, config.teams_commit, path)
        for path in config.submissions
    ]
    for repo, commit, path in files:
        url = f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{repo}/{commit}/{path}"
        (out / Path(path).name).write_bytes(download(url))
    sources: dict[str, object] = {
        "files": [
            {"repo": repo, "commit": commit, "path": path}
            for repo, commit, path in files
        ],
        "accessed": dt.date.today().isoformat(),
    }
    (out / "sources.json").write_text(json.dumps(sources, indent=2) + "\n")
    return sources

def asof_sums(
    triangle: pd.DataFrame, dates: Sequence[str], weeks: int = 8
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the 7-day sums as each nowcast date's data gave them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        Counts by Meldedatum and report date.
    dates : sequence of str
        Nowcast dates.
    weeks : int
        How far back the sums go, from each nowcast date.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `origin` (the nowcast date), `location` (the place),
        `target_end_date`, every day from `weeks` weeks before the
        nowcast date to it, and `total`, the sum reported by the nowcast
        date.
    """
    cols = ["origin", "location", "target_end_date", "total"]
    if not dates:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=cols)
    first = dt.date.fromisoformat(min(dates)) - dt.timedelta(weeks=weeks)
    ends = pd.date_range(first, max(dates), freq="D").date.astype(str)
    sums = hub_target(triangle, list(ends))
    sums = sums.loc[sums["vintage"].isin(set(dates))].rename(
        columns={"vintage": "origin"}
    )
    back = pd.to_datetime(sums["origin"]) - pd.to_datetime(
        sums["target_end_date"]
    )
    keep = back.dt.days <= 7 * weeks
    return sums.loc[keep, cols].reset_index(drop=True)

def germany_forecasts(
    models: Sequence[str],
    triangle: pd.DataFrame,
    dates: Sequence[str],
    n_samples: int,
    seed: int,
    tasks_dir: Path | None = None,
    horizons: Sequence[int] = HORIZONS,
    max_delay: int | None = None,
    timings: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    targets: Sequence[str] = ("7day",),
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Nowcast each date with each model, as quantiles at the hub's levels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    models : sequence of str
        Registered model names.
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        Counts by Meldedatum and report date
        (`nowcastgermany.data.read_triangle`).
    dates : sequence of str
        Nowcast dates.
    n_samples, seed : int
        Samples per forecast where the quantiles come from samples, and
        their seed, the same for every model.
    tasks_dir : pathlib.Path, optional
        A store of each date's tasks (`<date>.pkl`): read where it holds
        one, else built and written to it. The tasks are the same for
        every checkpoint, so they are built once (`checkpoint.german_tasks_dir`
        keys the store on what they are built from).
    horizons : sequence of int
        Days from each nowcast date to the end of each 7-day sum, the
        hub's 0 to -28 (`HORIZONS`) by default; days after it are
        forecasts (`nowcastgermany.data.nowcast_tasks`).
    max_delay : int, optional
        The truth's delay (`GermanyConfig.truth_delay`): the models see
        only the counts reported within it (`nowcastgermany.data.within_delay`),
        so they forecast the count the truth holds, not the eventual one.
        A `tasks_dir` must then be keyed on it.
    timings : list, optional
        Given, a row is appended for each model and date: `model`,
        `origin`, `stage` (`forecast`) and `seconds`; and one for each
        Chronos-2 model's batched pass over every date (`stage`
        `prefetch`, `origin` empty).
    targets : sequence of str
        Views of `TARGETS` to forecast. `daily` rows are each day's count,
        from the same forecast as the 7-day sums, as a model's own
        quantiles of its daily count rows
        (`FoundationModel.daily_quantiles`); a model without them gives
        none.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per quantile: `model`, `target`, `origin` (the nowcast date),
        `location` (the place), `target_end_date`, `horizon` (days),
        `quantile` and `value`, at `FORECAST_LEVELS`
        (`nowcasteval.marginals.forecast_quantiles`).
    """
    if max_delay is not None:
        triangle = within_delay(triangle, max_delay)
    built = [get_model(m) for m in models]
    # Chronos-2 is predicted for every date's tasks in a few batched passes,
    # so it needs them all at once. Each task holds its own copy of the
    # release history, so other models build one date's tasks at a time.
    tasks: dict[str, list[ForecastTask]] = {}
    if any(isinstance(m, FoundationModel) for m in built):
        tasks = {
            d: _tasks(triangle, d, n_samples, seed, tasks_dir, horizons)
            for d in dates
        }
        every = [t for ts in tasks.values() for t in ts]
        built = [
            _timed_prefetch(name, m, every, timings)
            if isinstance(m, FoundationModel)
            else m
            for name, m in zip(models, built, strict=True)
        ]
        # The loop pops each date's tasks, which frees them only once this
        # list no longer holds them.
        del every
    keys = [
        "model", "target", "origin", "location", "target_end_date", "horizon"
    ]  # fmt: skip
    daily = "daily" in targets
    frames = []
    for date in dates:
        mine = tasks.pop(date, None)
        if mine is None:
            mine = _tasks(triangle, date, n_samples, seed, tasks_dir, horizons)
        spent = dict.fromkeys(models, 0.0)
        for task in mine:
            for name, model in zip(models, built, strict=True):
                start = time.perf_counter()
                at = forecast_quantiles(
                    model, task, FORECAST_LEVELS, n_samples, seed
                )
                spent[name] += time.perf_counter() - start
                if at.empty:
                    continue
                # `hub_forecasts` moves rows to the hub's dates and places,
                # carrying each row's level where it carries a sample.
                moved = hub_forecasts(
                    at.rename(columns={"quantile": "sample"}), task, date
                )
                frames.append(
                    moved.rename(
                        columns={
                            "forecast_date": "origin",
                            "sample": "quantile",
                        }
                    ).assign(target="7day")
                )
        if daily:
            frames += _daily_rows(models, built, mine, date)
        if timings is not None:
            timings += [
                {"model": m, "origin": date, "stage": "forecast", "seconds": t}
                for m, t in spent.items()
            ]
    if not frames:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=[*keys, "quantile", "value"])
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    return out.sort_values([*keys, "quantile"], kind="stable")[
        [*keys, "quantile", "value"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

    triangle: pd.DataFrame, days: Sequence[str], truth_delay: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each place's count of each day as reported $D$ days later.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        Counts by Meldedatum and report date.
    days : sequence of str
        The days.
    truth_delay : int
        $D$.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `location` (each place of `PLACE_NAMES`), `target_end_date` (the
        day), `truth` and `truth_vintage` (the day plus $D$); `truth` is
        missing where the data hold no report that late.
    """
    places = triangle["location"].where(
        triangle["age_group"] == ALL_AGES, triangle["age_group"]
    )
    keep = places.isin(set(PLACE_NAMES)) & (
        (triangle["age_group"] == ALL_AGES) | (triangle["location"] == GERMANY)
    )
    rows = within_delay(
        triangle.loc[keep & triangle["reference_date"].isin(set(days))],
        truth_delay,
    )
    last = rows.sort_values("report_date").drop_duplicates(
        ["location", "age_group", "reference_date"], keep="last"
    )
    owner = last["location"].where(
        last["age_group"] == ALL_AGES, last["age_group"]
    )
    counts = dict(
        zip(
            zip(owner, last["reference_date"], strict=True),
            last["confirm"].astype(float),
            strict=True,
        )
    )
    final = str(triangle["report_date"].max())
    out = []
    for place in sorted(set(places.loc[keep])):
        for day in days:
            by = dt.date.fromisoformat(day) + dt.timedelta(days=truth_delay)
            seen = by.isoformat() <= final
            out.append(

def with_truth(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame, triangle: pd.DataFrame, truth_delay: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add each forecast's truth: the sum as reported $D$ days after it ends.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        `germany_forecasts` or `team_forecasts` output.
    triangle : pandas.DataFrame
        Counts by Meldedatum and report date.
    truth_delay : int
        $D$, the days after a sum ends that its truth is reported by.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `forecasts` with `truth` and `truth_vintage` (the report date of
        the truth), missing for sums with no data $D$ days after them.
    """
    on = ["location", "target_end_date"]
    daily = (
        forecasts["target"] == "daily"
        if "target" in forecasts
        else pd.Series(False, index=forecasts.index)
    )
    parts = []
    sums = forecasts.loc[~daily]
    ends = sorted(set(sums["target_end_date"]))
    if ends:
        truth = rolling_truth(hub_target(triangle, ends), truth_delay)
        parts.append(sums.merge(truth, on=on, how="left"))
    days = forecasts.loc[daily]
    if not days.empty:
        truth = daily_truth(
            triangle, sorted(set(days["target_end_date"])), truth_delay
        )
        parts.append(days.merge(truth, on=on, how="left"))
    if not parts:
        return forecasts.assign(truth=np.nan, truth_vintage=None)
    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

def truth_context(
    triangle: pd.DataFrame, config: GermanyConfig
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the truth the plots show, from `plot_start` on.

    Each place's daily count and 7-day sum of every day from
    `GermanyConfig.plot_start` to the last development nowcast date, as
    reported the truth delay after it, as the scores' truth
    (`with_truth`). Days with no report that late have no row.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `location`, `target` (`7day` or `daily`), `target_end_date`,
        `truth` and `truth_vintage`.
    """
    last = min(
        pd.Timestamp(nowcast_dates(config)[-1]),
        pd.Timestamp(triangle["report_date"].max())
        - pd.Timedelta(days=config.truth_delay),
    )
    days = [
        d.date().isoformat() for d in pd.date_range(config.plot_start, last)
    ]
    week = rolling_truth(hub_target(triangle, days), config.truth_delay)
    day = daily_truth(triangle, days, config.truth_delay)
    cols = ["location", "target", "target_end_date", "truth", "truth_vintage"]
    out = pd.concat(
        [week.assign(target="7day"), day.assign(target="daily")],
        ignore_index=True,
    )[cols]
    return out.loc[out["truth"].notna()].reset_index(drop=True)

def score_germany(forecasts: pd.DataFrame, truth_delay: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score quantile forecasts on their truth, as the hub scored them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        `with_truth` output.
    truth_delay : int
        $D$, which names the target.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per forecast with a truth: `model`, `target`
        (`"<D>-day"`), `origin`, `truth_vintage`, `location`,
        `target_end_date`, `horizon` (days), `truth`, `SCORE_COLUMNS` and
        `pool` (the paper's level, `national`, `states` or `age`).
    """
    cols = [*_KEYS, "target_end_date", "horizon", "truth", *SCORE_COLUMNS]
    rows = forecasts.dropna(subset=["truth"]).assign(
        target=f"{truth_delay}-day"
    )
    if rows.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=[*cols, "pool"])
    truth = rows[
        ["location", "target_end_date", "truth_vintage", "truth"]
    ].drop_duplicates()
    keys = [*_KEYS, "target_end_date"]
    level_of = rows["quantile"].round(6)
    scores = score_quantiles(
        rows.loc[level_of.isin(QUANTILE_LEVELS)].drop(columns="truth"),
        truth,
        keys,
        QUANTILE_LEVELS,
    )
    # The 90% interval, where the forecast has its levels (ours do; the
    # hub's teams' do not).
    outer = rows.loc[level_of.isin(OUTER_LEVELS)].pivot_table(
        index=keys, columns="quantile", values="value", aggfunc="first"
    )
    outer = outer.rename(columns=lambda q: round(float(q), 6))
    if set(OUTER_LEVELS) <= set(outer.columns):
        lo, hi = (outer[q] for q in OUTER_LEVELS)
        scores = scores.merge(
            pd.DataFrame({"lo": lo, "hi": hi}).reset_index(),
            on=keys,
            how="left",
        )
        inside = (scores["lo"] <= scores["truth"]) & (
            scores["truth"] <= scores["hi"]
        )
        scores["coverage_90"] = inside.astype(float).where(
            scores["lo"].notna() & scores["hi"].notna()
        )
    else:
        scores["coverage_90"] = np.nan
    scores["pool"] = scores["location"].map(level)
    return scores[[*cols, "pool"]]

def team_forecasts(
    submissions: pd.DataFrame, dates: Sequence[str] | None = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the hub teams' quantile nowcasts at our horizons.

    RKI's quantiles above `_RKI_ERROR` are replaced by its -1 day nowcast
    and Epiforecasts' missing 10% quantiles are filled (`_fill_tenth`), as
    the paper does. Nothing else is filled. Quantiles that cross are
    sorted within their forecast.

    Parameters
    ----------
    submissions : pandas.DataFrame
        `read_submissions` output.
    dates : sequence of str, optional
        The nowcast dates kept. All if None.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model` (the paper's name, `TEAM_NAMES`), `origin` (the
        forecast date), `location` (the place, as in `PLACE_NAMES`),
        `target_end_date`, `horizon` (days, as `HORIZONS`), `quantile` and
        `value`, for the places in `PLACE_NAMES`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a team is not in `TEAM_NAMES`.
    """
    rows = submissions.loc[submissions["type"] == "quantile", list(_SUBMISSION)]
    if dates is not None:
        rows = rows.loc[rows["forecast_date"].isin(set(dates))]
    unknown = set(rows["model"]) - set(TEAM_NAMES)
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"Teams with no name in TEAM_NAMES: {sorted(unknown)}")
    rows = rows.assign(model=rows["model"].map(TEAM_NAMES))
    targets = {f"{h} day ahead inc hosp": h for h in HORIZONS}
    rows = _fix_rki(rows)
    rows = _fill_tenth(rows.loc[rows["target"].isin(set(targets))])
    place = rows["location"].where(
        rows["age_group"] == ALL_AGES, rows["age_group"]
    )
    out = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "model": rows["model"],
            "origin": rows["forecast_date"],
            "location": place,
            "target_end_date": rows["target_end_date"],
            "horizon": rows["target"].map(targets),
            "quantile": rows["quantile"],
            "value": rows["value"],
        }
    )
    out = out.loc[out["location"].isin(set(PLACE_NAMES))]
    # Under 1% of the submitted forecasts have quantiles that cross. Their
    # values are sorted so each forecast is a distribution.
    ids = ["model", "origin", "location", "target_end_date"]
    out = out.sort_values([*ids, "quantile"])
    out["value"] = out.groupby(ids)["value"].transform(np.sort)
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def relative_scores(
    scores: pd.DataFrame, by: Sequence[str], baseline: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each model's pairwise relative scores and its own means.

    The relative scores are `nowcasteval.scoring.pairwise_skill`, so
    models that forecast different nowcasts (hub teams that missed
    dates) compare fairly. The means are over each model's own
    forecasts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        `score_germany` output, for our models and the teams.
    by : sequence of str
        Columns of a cell other than `model`.
    baseline : str
        The model the relative scores are scaled to, such as
        `GermanyConfig.baseline`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per cell and model: `n` (its forecasts), `rounds` (its
        nowcast dates), `wis`, `rel_wis`, `ae_median`, `rel_ae_median`,
        and the coverage of the 50% and 95% intervals.
    """
    by = list(by)
    match = ("target", "origin", "truth_vintage", "location", "target_end_date")
    rel = pairwise_skill(
        scores,
        baseline,
        by=by,
        metrics=("wis", "ae_median"),
        match_on=match,
        rounds="origin",
    )
    mean_cols = ["wis", "ae_median", "coverage_50", "coverage_95"]
    means = scores.groupby([*by, "model"])[mean_cols].mean().reset_index()
    rel = rel.merge(means, on=[*by, "model"]).rename(
        columns={
            "relative_wis": "rel_wis",
            "relative_ae_median": "rel_ae_median",
        }
    )
    cols = ["n", "rounds", "wis", "rel_wis", "ae_median", "rel_ae_median"]
    return rel[[*by, "model", *cols, "coverage_50", "coverage_95"]]

def model_styles(
    models: Sequence[str], ours: Collection[str]
) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Return each model's light colour, dark colour and dash.

    Our models keep their own (`model_style`). The hub teams take the
    colours ours leave free in turn, solid and then dashed, so no two
    models look the same.

    Parameters
    ----------
    models : sequence of str
        Every model shown, in order.
    ours : collection of str
        Our models.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Model to its light colour, dark colour and dash.
    """
    out = {m: model_style(m, models) for m in models if m in ours}
    used = {MODEL_STYLE[m][0] for m in out if m in MODEL_STYLE}
    free = [i for i in range(len(MODEL_COLOURS["light"])) if i not in used]
    dashes = list(DASHES.values())
    teams = [m for m in models if m not in ours]
    for k, m in enumerate(teams):
        slot = free[k % len(free)]
        out[m] = (
            MODEL_COLOURS["light"][slot],
            MODEL_COLOURS["dark"][slot],
            dashes[(k // len(free)) % len(dashes)],
        )
    return {m: out[m] for m in models}

def held_out_leaks(paths: Iterable[Path], split_date: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the held-out dates the German page's files name.

    A JSON file may name no date on or after the split date. A text
    file (Markdown or HTML) may name the split date itself, as the page's
    prose does, but no later date.

    Parameters
    ----------
    paths : iterable of pathlib.Path
        The page's files: the summary and explorer JSON, the snippets or
        the built page.
    split_date : str
        The first held-out nowcast date.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        One line per file and date found, empty if none.
    """
    found = []
    for path in paths:
        text = path.read_text()
        if path.suffix == ".json":
            hits = {
                (where, d)
                for where, d in _json_dates(json.loads(text), "")
                if d >= split_date
            }
        else:
            hits = {("", d) for d in _DATE.findall(text) if d > split_date}
        found += [f"{path}{where}: {d}" for where, d in sorted(hits)]
    return found

def germany_explorer(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    asof: pd.DataFrame | None,
    config: GermanyConfig,
    models: list[str],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return the forecast explorer's data for the German nowcasts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        `nowcastgermany backtest` and `nowcastgermany teams` forecasts,
        with truth.
    asof : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        `nowcastgermany asof` output.
    config : GermanyConfig
        Gives the dates, the plot spacing and the hidden models.
    models : list of str
        Models in order, which sets their colours (`model_styles`).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `explorer_data` output, at every `plot_every`-th development date.
    """
    rounds = set(nowcast_dates(config)[:: config.plot_every])
    rows = forecasts.loc[
        forecasts["origin"].isin(rounds) & forecasts["model"].isin(models)
    ]
    wide = (
        rows.assign(quantile=rows["quantile"].round(6))
        .pivot_table(
            index=["model", "origin", "location", "target_end_date"],
            columns="quantile",
            values="value",
            aggfunc="first",
        )[list(_BANDS.values())]
        .set_axis(list(_BANDS), axis=1)
        .reset_index()
    )
    styles = model_styles(models, config.models)
    shown = [m for m in models if m in set(wide["model"])]
    wide["model"] = pd.Categorical(wide["model"], shown)
    wide = wide.sort_values(["model", "origin", "location"])
    wide = wide.assign(
        model=wide["model"].astype(str),
        ours=wide["model"].isin(set(config.models)),
        reference_date=wide["origin"],
    )
    truth = forecasts[["location", "target_end_date", "truth"]].dropna()
    truth = truth.drop_duplicates(["location", "target_end_date"])
    target = truth.rename(columns={"truth": "total"}).assign(
        kind="real", vintage="truth"
    )
    seen = None
    if asof is not None:
        seen = asof.rename(columns={"origin": "reference_date"})
    return explorer_data(
        wide,
        target,
        PLACE_NAMES,
        0,
        {m: styles[m] for m in shown},
        truth_vintage="truth",
        hidden=config.hidden,
        level_of=lambda x: LEVELS[level(x)],
        levels=tuple(LEVELS.values()),
        outer="95%",
        unit="hospitalisations",
        complete_through=str(truth["target_end_date"].max()),
        data_label=f"reported {config.truth_delay} days on",
        asof=seen,
    )

def germany_page(
    fig: Path,
    gen: Path,
    results: Path,
    config: GermanyConfig,
    shown: Callable[[Iterable[str]], list[str]],
) -> None:
    """Write the German nowcast benchmark page's table and summaries.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fig : pathlib.Path
        Where the summary JSON goes.
    gen : pathlib.Path
        Where the Markdown snippets go.
    results : pathlib.Path
        `nowcastgermany backtest` output (`scores.csv.gz`, `forecasts.csv.gz`),
        and if they have been run `nowcastgermany teams` output (`teams.csv.gz`,
        `teams-forecasts.csv.gz`) and `nowcastgermany asof` output
        (`asof.csv.gz`). If the scores are missing, the page says the
        benchmark has not been run.
    config : GermanyConfig
        The benchmark's source, which the page credits.
    shown : callable
        Keeps the models the page shows, in order (the site's
        `bdbvhub.reporting.site.site_models`).
    """
    url = f"https://github.com/{config.repo}/blob/{config.commit}"
    teams_url = (
        f"https://github.com/{config.teams_repo}/blob/{config.teams_commit}"
    )
    files = ", ".join(f"[`{p}`]({teams_url}/{p})" for p in config.submissions)
    _write(
        gen / "germany-sources.md",
        f"- The reporting triangle: [`{config.triangle}`]"
        f"({url}/{config.triangle}) in {config.repo} at "
        f"`{config.commit[:7]}`.\n"
        f"- The hub teams' nowcasts: {files} in {config.teams_repo} at "
        f"`{config.teams_commit[:7]}` (MIT).\n",
    )
    _write(gen / "germany-ft.md", _ft_note(results))
    if not (results / "scores.csv.gz").exists():
        for name in _PAGES[:-1]:
            _write(
                gen / name, "Not run yet: `task nowcastgermany:benchmark`.\n"
            )
        return
    scores = _read(results, ("scores.csv.gz", "teams.csv.gz"), shown)
    assert scores is not None
    scores = _shared_cells(_development(scores, config))
    _refuse_held_out(scores, config.split_date)
    # Each sum has one truth, reported `truth_delay` days after it ends,
    # up to 40 days into the held-out half. The page names the truth,
    # not its report date.
    scores = scores.assign(truth_vintage=f"{config.truth_delay}-day truth")
    forecasts = _read(
        results, ("forecasts.csv.gz", "teams-forecasts.csv.gz"), shown
    )
    run = set(scores["model"])
    if forecasts is not None:
        run |= set(forecasts["model"])
    # One list for every view, so each model keeps its colour.
    models = [m for m in [*config.models, *TEAM_NAMES.values()] if m in run]
    write_score_chart(
        fig / "scoresummary-germany-latest.json",
        summary_rows(
            scores,
            models,
            model_styles(models, config.models),
            PLACE_NAMES,
            baseline=config.baseline,
            metrics=METRICS,
            default_on=[m for m in models if m not in config.hidden],
            pool_of=level,
            pool_labels=LEVELS,
        ),
    )
    srcs = {"latest": "../figures/scoresummary-germany-latest.json"}
    table = relative_scores(scores, ("pool",), config.baseline)
    table["pool"] = pd.Categorical(table["pool"], list(LEVELS))
    # The summary above gives the absolute scores, so the table fits the
    # page with the relative ones.
    table = table.sort_values(["pool", "rel_wis"]).drop(
        columns=["wis", "ae_median"]
    )
    _write(
        gen / "germany-scores.md",
        f"Nowcast dates before {config.split_date} only; the later half "
        "is held out for the paper.\n\n"
        + summary_html(srcs, "Overall scores by level")
        + "\n"
        + sortable_table(table, digits=3),
    )
    if forecasts is None:
        _write(
            gen / "germany-nowcasts.md",
            "Not run yet: `task nowcastgermany:benchmark`.\n",
        )
    else:
        forecasts = _development(forecasts, config)
        _refuse_held_out(forecasts, config.split_date)
        write_explorer(
            fig / "explorer-germany.json",
            germany_explorer(
                forecasts,
                _read(results, ("asof.csv.gz",), shown),
                config,
                models,
            ),
        )
        _write(
            gen / "germany-nowcasts.md",
            explorer_html(
                "../figures/explorer-germany.json",
                "German nowcasts",
                summary=srcs,
            ),
        )
    _write(
        gen / "germany-horizon.md",
        summary_html(srcs, "Scores by horizon", view="horizon"),
    )
    _write(
        gen / "germany-place.md",
        summary_html(srcs, "Scores by place", view="place"),
    )
    written = [
        fig / "scoresummary-germany-latest.json",
        *[p for p in [fig / "explorer-germany.json"] if p.exists()],
        *[gen / name for name in (*_PAGES, "germany-ft.md")],
    ]
    leaks = held_out_leaks(written, config.split_date)
    if leaks:
        raise ValueError(
            "The German page names held-out dates: " + "; ".join(leaks[:5])
        )

def check_site(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Check the built site's German page names no held-out nowcast date.

    The `germany-site-check SITE [--config
    packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml]` command,
    run from the repo root after `mkdocs build`. Reads the German page
    and its summary and explorer JSON (`held_out_leaks`) and returns 1,
    listing them, if any names a date on or after the split date (or
    after it, in the page's prose), or if one is not built.
    """
    import argparse

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=check_site.__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("site", type=Path, nargs="?", default=Path("_site"))
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml"),
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    split = load_germany_config(args.config).split_date
    files = [
        args.site / "germany" / "index.html",
        args.site / "figures" / "scoresummary-germany-latest.json",
        args.site / "figures" / "explorer-germany.json",
    ]
    missing = [str(f) for f in files if not f.exists()]
    if missing:
        print(f"Not built: {', '.join(missing)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    leaks = held_out_leaks(files, split)
    for leak in leaks:
        print(f"::error::held-out date on the German page: {leak}")
    if not leaks:
        print(f"The German page names no nowcast date from {split} on.")
    return 1 if leaks else 0

  • fetch: download the benchmark's data at the config's commits.
  • backtest: nowcast and score the benchmark with our models.

  • unit-publish: attach a released checkpoint's German unit to its release as the stored forecasts (publish_germany_unit).

def read_unit(cache: Path | str, label: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Stack a label's German unit files as the page scores them.

    The 7-day sums at the hub's nowcast horizons (0 days back or
    earlier), without the `target` column.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cache : pathlib.Path or str
        The score cache, with `<UNIT>/<label>/<date>.csv.gz`.
    label : str
        The checkpoint's label.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The rows.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the unit has no files.
    """
    root = Path(cache) / UNIT / label
    files = sorted(root.glob("20*.csv.gz"))
    if not files:
        raise ValueError(f"No German unit files in {root}.")
    dtype = {"origin": str, "truth_vintage": str, "target_end_date": str}
    rows = pd.concat(
        [pd.read_csv(f, dtype=dtype) for f in files], ignore_index=True
    )
    if "target" in rows:
        rows = rows.loc[rows["target"] == "7day"].drop(columns="target")
    return rows.loc[rows["horizon"] <= 0].reset_index(drop=True)

    tag = release_tag(label)

def development_rows(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    split_date: str,
    models: tuple[str, ...] = STORED_MODELS,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the models' forecasts, refusing any held-out date.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        `germany_forecasts` output with truth (`with_truth`), of any
        models.
    split_date : str
        The first held-out nowcast date (`GermanyConfig.split_date`).
    models : tuple of str
        The models kept.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The models' rows, sorted.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a row of the models has a nowcast date or a target end date on
        or after the split date, or there are none.
    """
    rows = forecasts.loc[forecasts["model"].isin(models)].copy()
    for col in ("origin", "target_end_date", "truth_vintage"):
        rows[col] = rows[col].astype(str)
    late = (rows["origin"] >= split_date) | (
        rows["target_end_date"] >= split_date
    )
    if late.any():
        first = rows.loc[late, "origin"].min()
        raise ValueError(
            f"{int(late.sum())} rows of {', '.join(models)} are held-out "
            f"(on or after {split_date}, from {first}); only development "
            "dates may be "
            "stored or shown."
        )
    if rows.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"No forecasts of {', '.join(models)}.")
    keys = [
        "model",
        "origin",
        "location",
        "target_end_date",
        "horizon",
        "quantile",
    ]
    return rows.sort_values(keys, kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)

docs.text:
Score each published Chronos-2 checkpoint.

Each checkpoint (release chronos-ft-<hash> or chronos-slots-<hash>) is a label, run beside reference (randomwalknowcast and zero-shot Chronos-2, ragged and complete). A label's units forecast and cache; table scores the caches into rows of evidence/checkpoint-scores.csv with rule = RULE:

  • germany: the development half of the German benchmark (packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml), quantile WIS and log WIS on each model's own quantiles (nowcastgermany.evaluation.germany_forecasts), by level.
  • held_out: the trainer's held-out loss from the release's settings.json (unit release).

BDBV is held out for the paper, so no BDBV rows are scored here.

A German unit splits its chunks of dates over SCORE_WORKERS worker processes (score_workers), its rule's threads; each chunk is forecast as one process would, so the rows are the same. On CUDA it forecasts in its own process, which holds the rule's one GPU. A worker exits when its coordinator does, which stops its workers on SIGTERM.

Relative scores divide by randomwalknowcast's on the cells every model and checkpoint of a level made. Every score comes from nowcasteval.scoring, as the paper's and the dashboard's do. Rows are keyed by checkpoint hash and run, with the checkpoint's outbreaks and grid.

Usage: python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint germany CACHE LABEL [SEGMENT] python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint release CACHE HASH python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint table CACHE EVIDENCE \ CHECKPOINTS HASH... python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint run TRAIN SCORES REFERENCE RUN OUT python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint daily TRAIN SCORES REFERENCE RUN OUT python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint horizons TRAIN SCORES REFERENCE RUN OUT python -m nowcastgermany.checkpoint compare OUT TABLE...

    """Return a checkpoint's run from its settings.

def matched(rows: pd.DataFrame, cell: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Keep, in each level, the cells every model and checkpoint made."""
    key = rows["model"] + "@" + rows["checkpoint"]
    out = []

        n = part.groupby(cell)["_k"].nunique()

def relative(
    rows: pd.DataFrame,
    study: str,
    metrics: tuple[str, str],
    baseline: str = BASELINE,
    target: str = "7day",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return mean scores relative to `baseline`, by level and model.

    With the mean WIS and its components, and coverage, where the rows
    have them. Rows are tagged with `target`.
    """
    widths = (*COVERAGE, *GERMANY_COVERAGE)
    extra = [
        "wis",
        *WIS_PARTS,
        *(f"coverage_{p}" for p in dict.fromkeys(widths)),
    ]
    extra = [c for c in extra if c in rows and c not in metrics]
    keys = ["level", "model", "checkpoint"]
    mean = rows.groupby(keys)[[*metrics, *extra]].mean()
    mean["n"] = rows.groupby(keys).size()
    origins = rows.groupby(keys)["origin"]
    mean["n_origins"] = origins.nunique()
    mean["first_origin"] = origins.min()
    mean["last_origin"] = origins.max()
    base = mean.xs((baseline, "zero-shot"), level=("model", "checkpoint"))
    at = mean.index.get_level_values("level")
    for m in metrics:
        mean[f"rel_{m}"] = mean[m] / base[m].reindex(at).to_numpy()
    out = mean.reset_index().assign(study=study, rule=RULE, target=target)
    return out.reindex(columns=COLUMNS)

def merge_evidence(old: pd.DataFrame, new: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add rule rows to the evidence, replacing the checkpoints' old ones.

    The rule's rows of checkpoints not in `new` are kept; rows of any
    other rule are dropped.
    """
    old = old.reindex(columns=COLUMNS)
    mine = set(new["checkpoint"].astype(str))
    old = old.loc[
        (old["rule"] == RULE) & ~old["checkpoint"].astype(str).isin(mine)

        drop=True

def german_tasks_dir(
    cache: Path,
    triangle: Path,
    n_samples: int,
    seed: int,
    max_delay: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Return the store of the German tasks every checkpoint scores.

    Keyed on what the tasks are built from: the triangle file's bytes,
    the task-building code (`nowcastgermany.data` and the
    `nowcastutils.dates` it uses),
    the fields of the `ForecastTask` they are pickled as, the draws and
    seed, and the longest delay the models see (`max_delay`).
    """
    import hashlib
    import inspect

    from nowcastgermany import data as dg
    from nowcastutils import base, dates

    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(triangle).open("rb") as f:
        for part in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 24), b""):
            h.update(part)
    for module in (dg, dates):
        h.update(inspect.getsource(module).encode())
    fields = [f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(base.ForecastTask)]
    h.update(repr(fields).encode())
    h.update(f"{n_samples}-{seed}".encode())
    if max_delay is not None:
        h.update(f"max_delay-{max_delay}".encode())
    return Path(cache) / GERMANY_UNIT / f"tasks-{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"

def worker_cores(cores: Sequence[int], index: int, workers: int) -> list[int]:
    """Return the cores of worker `index` of `workers`: its share of `cores`.

    Each worker takes its own slice, so none of their thread pools (XLA's
    sizes itself to every core it may use) crowds another's.
    """
    each = max(1, len(cores) // workers)
    at = (index % max(1, len(cores) // each)) * each
    return list(cores)[at : at + each]

Forecast each German development date, own quantiles with truth.

Each date is forecast at the German config's horizons (horizons): the hub's nowcast and the forecast days after it. The fine-tuned models load the release label names, or a run's own segment folder (<run>/train/n<N>) when given, cached as label. Its chunks of dates are split over score_workers() processes.

Source code in packages/nowcastgermany/src/nowcastgermany/checkpoint.py 
def germany_unit(cache: Path, label: str, segment: Path | None = None) -> None:
    """Forecast each German development date, own quantiles with truth.

    Each date is forecast at the German config's horizons (`horizons`):
    the hub's nowcast and the forecast days after it. The fine-tuned
    models load the release `label` names, or a run's own `segment`
    folder (`<run>/train/n<N>`) when given, cached as `label`. Its
    chunks of dates are split over `score_workers()` processes.
    """
    from nowcastgermany import evaluation as de
    from nowcastgermany.data import hub_triangle

    _pin(label, segment)
    config = de.load_germany_config(
        "packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml"
    )
    path = triangle_path(config)
    triangle = hub_triangle(path)
    # Built once for every checkpoint, then read back.
    tasks_dir = german_tasks_dir(
        cache, path, config.n_samples, config.seed, config.truth_delay
    )
    root = cache / GERMANY_UNIT / label
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    record_precision(root)
    dates = de.nowcast_dates(config, held_out=False)
    # The plots' truth from `plot_start`, shared by every unit.
    _write(
        de.truth_context(triangle, config),
        cache / GERMANY_UNIT / TRUTH_FILE,
    )
    last = max(config.horizons)
    models = list(label_models(label, layout=segment_layout(segment)))
    # A date's rows are kept only if forecast from this task store: the
    # tasks' building code is in its name (`german_tasks_dir`). The
    # reference's do not depend on a checkpoint, so each model's are also
    # keyed on its own code and the German config (`model_key`), and a
    # change redoes that model's rows alone.
    tasks = tasks_dir.name
    want = {
        m: f"{tasks}-{model_key(m)}" if label == REFERENCE else tasks
        for m in models
    }
    have = written(root)
    groups: dict[tuple[str, ...], list[str]] = {}
    for d in dates:
        full = not _reaches(root / f"{d}.csv.gz", last, config.targets)
        need = tuple(
            m
            for m in models
            if full or have.get((d, m), have.get((d, EVERY))) != want[m]
        )
        if need:
            groups.setdefault(need, []).append(d)
    # Rows of a model the label no longer runs (a renamed or dropped
    # model) go from every date, also those nothing is redone on.
    gone = {d for (d, m) in have if m != EVERY and m not in models}
    for d in sorted(gone - {d for ds in groups.values() for d in ds}):
        out = root / f"{d}.csv.gz"
        if out.exists():
            old = pd.read_csv(out)
            _write(old.loc[old["model"].isin(models)], out)
    # Dates are forecast `score_dates()` at a time, Chronos-2 predicted for
    # all of them in a few batched passes, and written one file a date so
    # a stopped run resumes. The chunks are the same however many workers
    # forecast them, so their rows are too.
    step = score_dates()
    chunks: list[Chunk] = [
        (need, ds[i : i + step])
        for need, ds in groups.items()
        for i in range(0, len(ds), step)
    ]
    unit = _Unit(root, tasks_dir, tuple(models))
    done = len(dates) - sum(len(c) for _, c in chunks)
    times = root / "timings.csv"
    start = time.monotonic()
    results = _chunk_results(
        unit, triangle, chunks, score_workers(), (label, segment, path)
    )
    # This process alone records the dates and their timings.
    for (need, chunk), timings in results:
        # Seconds by model and date, for the `benchmarks` target.
        pd.DataFrame(timings).assign(dates=len(chunk)).to_csv(
            times, mode="a", header=not times.exists(), index=False
        )
        for date in chunk:
            _record(root, date, {m: want[m] for m in need})
        done += len(chunk)
        print(
            f"germany {label} {len(chunk)} dates to {chunk[-1]} "
            f"({done}/{len(dates)}): {time.monotonic() - start:.0f} s",
            flush=True,
        )
    print(f"germany {label} done", flush=True)

def release_unit(cache: Path, label: str) -> None:
    """Fetch a release's settings.json, with its held-out sidecar if any."""
    from nowcastfoundation.forecaster import release_tag

    root = cache / "heldout"
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tag_ = release_tag(label)
    out = str(root / f"{label}.json")
    subprocess.run(
        ["gh", "release", "download", tag_, "-R", REPO, "-p", "settings.json",
         "-O", out, "--clobber"],
        check=True,
    )  # fmt: skip
    view = subprocess.run(
        ["gh", "release", "view", tag_, "-R", REPO, "--json", "assets"],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )  # fmt: skip
    release = json.loads(view.stdout)
    # Offloaded checkpoints keep their held-out losses in a sidecar.
    if SIDECAR in {a["name"] for a in release.get("assets", [])}:
        sidecar = root / f"{label}-{SIDECAR}"
        subprocess.run(
            ["gh", "release", "download", tag_, "-R", REPO, "-p", SIDECAR,
             "-O", str(sidecar), "--clobber"],
            check=True,
        )  # fmt: skip
        settings = json.loads(Path(out).read_text())
        merged = with_sidecar(settings, json.loads(sidecar.read_text()))
        Path(out).write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=1))

def germany_rows(
    folders: Mapping[str, Path],
    target: str = "7day",
    baseline: str = BASELINE,
    horizons: str = "nowcast",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the German development half's rule rows.

    `folders` gives each label's cached German unit. Rows are of the view
    `target` (`7day` or `daily`), relative to zero-shot `baseline`, on
    the part of the horizons `horizons` names (`HORIZON_PARTS`): by
    default the hub's, as the paper scores the teams.
    """
    from nowcastgermany import evaluation as de

    config = de.load_germany_config(
        "packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml"
    )
    parts = []
    for label, folder in folders.items():
        fc = _cached(folder, target)
        if fc is None or fc.empty:
            continue
        keep = HORIZON_PARTS[horizons](fc["horizon"])
        fc = fc.loc[(fc["origin"] < config.split_date) & keep]
        nat = de.score_germany(fc, config.truth_delay)
        logged = fc.assign(
            value=np.log1p(fc["value"].clip(lower=0)),
            truth=np.log1p(fc["truth"]),
        )
        log = de.score_germany(logged, config.truth_delay)
        log = log[["model", *GERMANY_CELL, "wis"]].rename(
            columns={"wis": "log_wis"}
        )
        sc = nat.merge(log, on=["model", *GERMANY_CELL])
        parts.append(tag(sc, label))
    if not parts:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=COLUMNS)
    sc = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True).rename(columns={"pool": "level"})
    out = relative(
        matched(sc, GERMANY_CELL),
        "germany",
        ("wis", "log_wis"),
        baseline,
        target,
    )
    return _with_precision(out, folders)

def table(
    cache: Path, evidence: Path, checkpoints: Path, hashes: Sequence[str]
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score the caches of `hashes` and the reference into the tables.

    Rows of other rules, and of this rule for other checkpoints, are kept.
    """
    meta = {}
    for h in hashes:
        settings = json.loads((cache / "heldout" / f"{h}.json").read_text())
        meta[h] = (settings, *outbreaks_and_grid(settings))
    labels = [REFERENCE, *hashes]
    # BDBV is held out for the paper: no BDBV rows are computed, and
    # those already in `evidence` are kept.
    new = pd.concat(
        [
            germany_rows({lb: cache / GERMANY_UNIT / lb for lb in labels}),
            *(held_out_rows(h, m[0]) for h, m in meta.items()),
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
    new["outbreaks"] = new["checkpoint"].map({h: m[1] for h, m in meta.items()})
    new["outbreaks"] = new["outbreaks"].fillna(0).astype(int)
    new["grid"] = new["checkpoint"].map({h: m[2] for h, m in meta.items()})
    runs = {h: run_of(m[0]) for h, m in meta.items()}
    new["run"] = new["checkpoint"].map(runs).fillna("zero-shot")
    new["chosen"] = chosen(new)
    merged = merge_evidence(_existing(evidence, COLUMNS), new)
    merged.round(4).to_csv(evidence, index=False)
    ck = _existing(checkpoints, ["checkpoint", "outbreaks", "grid"])
    add = pd.DataFrame(
        [(h, m[1], m[2]) for h, m in meta.items()],
        columns=["checkpoint", "outbreaks", "grid"],
    )
    ck = pd.concat(
        [ck.loc[~ck["checkpoint"].astype(str).isin(add["checkpoint"])], add],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
    ck.to_csv(checkpoints, index=False)
    return new

def daily_table(
    train: Path, scores: Path, reference: Path, run: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a run's checkpoints on both German views, for the SI.

    Each saved segment's relative WIS on the 7-day sums (against the
    config's `baseline`) and on the daily counts (against its
    `daily_baseline`), by level, in the comparison layout (`set`, `run`,
    `outbreaks`, `score`) of `paperpipe.evidence.comparison_figure`.
    """
    from nowcastgermany import evaluation as de

    config = de.load_germany_config(
        "packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml"
    )
    folders = {REFERENCE: Path(reference)} | {
        d.name: Path(scores) / d.name
        for d in _segments(train)
        if (Path(scores) / d.name).is_dir()
    }
    outbreaks = {
        d.name: outbreaks_and_grid(
            json.loads((d / "settings.json").read_text())
        )[0]
        for d in _segments(train)
    }
    bases = {"7day": config.baseline, "daily": config.daily_baseline}
    parts = []
    for target in config.targets:
        rows = germany_rows(folders, target, bases[target])
        rows = rows.loc[rows["checkpoint"].isin(outbreaks)]
        parts.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "set": f"Germany, {VIEWS[target]}, " + rows["level"],
                    "run": run,
                    "outbreaks": rows["checkpoint"].map(outbreaks),
                    "score": rows["rel_wis"],
                }
            )
        )
    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> None:
    """Run one unit, or rebuild the tables."""
    if len(argv) < 3:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
    study, cache = argv[0], Path(argv[1])
    if study == "germany" and len(argv) <= 4:
        segment = Path(argv[3]) if len(argv) == 4 else None
        germany_unit(cache, argv[2], segment)
    elif study == "release":
        release_unit(cache, argv[2])
    elif study == "run" and len(argv) == 6:
        out = run_table(cache, Path(argv[2]), Path(argv[3]), argv[4])
        out.round(4).to_csv(argv[5], index=False)
    elif study == "daily" and len(argv) == 6:
        out = daily_table(cache, Path(argv[2]), Path(argv[3]), argv[4])
        out.round(4).to_csv(argv[5], index=False)
    elif study == "horizons" and len(argv) == 6:
        out = horizon_table(cache, Path(argv[2]), Path(argv[3]), argv[4])
        out.round(4).to_csv(argv[5], index=False)
    elif study == "compare" and len(argv) >= 3:
        tables = [pd.read_csv(p) for p in argv[2:]]
        comparison(tables).to_csv(cache, index=False)
    elif study == "table" and len(argv) >= 4:
        new = table(cache, Path(argv[2]), Path(argv[3]), argv[4:])
        print(new.round(3).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
    else:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)

    data: str,
    config_path: str = "packages/nowcastgermany/config/germany.toml",
    dates: list[str] | None = None,

    r"""Score both pairings on the German development half.

    Each nowcast date's states tasks (with Germany their sum) and age
    groups tasks, one pair per date, are forecast as the German
    benchmark does (`nowcastgermany.data.nowcast_tasks`, `hub_forecasts`).
    The walks have weekly steps, so they forecast the 7-day sums ending on
    Saturdays (`hub_weeks`). The truth
    is the sum reported the config's truth delay after it ends.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : str
        The German data directory.
    config_path : str
        The German config.
    dates : list of str, optional
        Only these nowcast dates (a block of a chunked run).

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `variant_scores` rows of every model, variant, date and level.
    pandas.DataFrame
        The rolling $\rho_p$ of each model and task (`RHO_COLUMNS`): its
        copula record, with `origin` the nowcast date and `level` its
        places (`states` or `ages`).
    """
    cfg = de.load_germany_config(config_path)
    triangle = hub_triangle(Path(data) / Path(cfg.triangle).name)
    run = de.nowcast_dates(cfg) if dates is None else list(dates)
    levels = dict.fromkeys(AGE_GROUPS, "ages")
    frames, fits = [], []
    # The models see the counts the truth holds (`within_delay`).
    seen = within_delay(triangle, cfg.truth_delay)
    for date in run:
        for task in map(
            hub_weeks, nowcast_tasks(seen, date, cfg.n_samples, cfg.seed)
        ):
            level = (
                "ages" if set(task.locations) & set(AGE_GROUPS) else "states"
            )
            for name in MODELS:
                drawn, fit = variant_forecasts(name, task)
                if fit is not None:
                    fits.append({**fit, "origin": date, "level": level})
                if not drawn:
                    continue
                moved = {
                    label: hub_forecasts(
                        s.assign(model=name, as_of=np.nan), task, date
                    )
                    for label, s in drawn.items()
                }
                ends = sorted(
                    set(next(iter(moved.values()))["target_end_date"])
                )
                truth = rolling_truth(
                    hub_target(triangle, ends), cfg.truth_delay
                )
                for label, s in moved.items():
                    frames.append(
                        variant_scores(
                            s,
                            truth,
                            study="germany",
                            model=name,
                            variant=label,
                            origin=date,
                            levels={
                                **levels,
                                **{
                                    p: "states"
                                    for p in set(s["location"])
                                    if p not in levels and p != "DE"
                                },
                            },
                        )
                    )
    rho = pd.DataFrame(fits, columns=list(RHO_COLUMNS))
    if not frames:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=list(SCORE_COLUMNS)), rho
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    # Germany's provinces are its states.
    out["level"] = out["level"].replace({"provinces": "states"})
    return out, rho

def window(first_date: str, truth_delay: int) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return the last report date used and the last date with truth.

    Reports up to the day before `first_date`, the first scored German
    nowcast date; a count is truth once `truth_delay` days have passed,
    as the benchmark takes its truth.
    """
    as_of = dt.date.fromisoformat(first_date) - dt.timedelta(days=1)
    truth = as_of - dt.timedelta(days=truth_delay)
    return as_of.isoformat(), truth.isoformat()

def cut_dates(first: str, truth_until: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return every nowcast date whose horizon ends by `truth_until`."""
    last = dt.date.fromisoformat(truth_until) - dt.timedelta(weeks=AHEAD_WEEKS)
    day, out = dt.date.fromisoformat(first), []
    while day <= last:
        out.append(day.isoformat())
        day += dt.timedelta(days=1)
    return out

def german_counts(wide: pd.DataFrame, as_of: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the German hub triangle's counts as reported by `as_of`.

    Each change of `value_0d` to `value_80d` is reported on its Meldedatum
    plus its delay; the change after 80 days is left out. States (all
    ages) and Germany's age groups are kept, named as the German tasks
    name them (`nowcastgermany.data.place_code`); Germany is their sum.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `location`, `reference_date`, `report_date` and `count`, as
        `finetune.training_block` reads.
    """
    long = de.hub_changes(wide)
    long = long.loc[long["delay"] <= 80]
    states = (long["age_group"] == de.ALL_AGES) & (
        long["location"] != de.GERMANY
    )
    ages = (long["location"] == de.GERMANY) & (long["age_group"] != de.ALL_AGES)
    long = long.loc[states | ages]
    report = pd.to_datetime(long["date"]) + pd.to_timedelta(long["delay"], "D")
    out = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "location": [
                de.place_code(loc, age)
                for loc, age in zip(
                    long["location"], long["age_group"], strict=True
                )
            ],
            "reference_date": long["date"].astype(str),
            "report_date": report.dt.date.astype(str),
            "count": long["change"].astype("int64"),
        }
    )
    out = out.loc[out["report_date"] <= as_of]
    return out.sort_values(
        ["location", "reference_date", "report_date"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

def german_blocks(
    counts: pd.DataFrame,
    cuts: list[str],
    truth_until: str,
    first: int = 0,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the training blocks of the German data at nowcast dates.

    Each cut is laid out as the German tasks lay it out, on its real
    dates: every report date up to it is a release, and Germany is the
    country (`parent` exact). Each of `PLACES` gives a
    block by `finetune.training_block`, at a lag taken in turn from
    `LAGS` (from cut `first` on), padded as the simulated blocks are.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a cut's horizon ends after `truth_until`.
    """
    places = sorted(counts["location"].unique())
    states = [p for p in places if "-A" not in p]
    ages = [p for p in places if "-A" in p]
    leaves = {"national": states, "states": states, "ages": ages}
    out = []
    for i, cut in enumerate(cuts, start=first):
        end = dt.date.fromisoformat(cut) + dt.timedelta(weeks=AHEAD_WEEKS)
        if end.isoformat() > truth_until:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cut {cut} needs truth to {end}, past the truth date "
                f"{truth_until}"
            )
        cutoffs = sorted(d for d in counts["report_date"].unique() if d <= cut)
        for j, which in enumerate(PLACES):
            view = (NATIONAL,)
            if which != "national":
                view = (NATIONAL, *leaves[which])
            own = counts.loc[counts["location"].isin(leaves[which])]
            block = training_block(
                own,
                SOURCE,
                view,
                cutoffs,
                max_lag=LAGS[(i + j) % len(LAGS)],
            )
            if block is None or block["start"] < 2:
                continue
            padded = ft._pad(
                block,
                ft.CONTEXT,
                ft.LOSS_HORIZON_DAYS,
                ft.DAYS_PER_STEP[SOURCE],
            )
            levels = ft.target_levels(view)
            padded["levels"] = tuple(levels[k] for k in block["target_places"])
            padded["places"] = view
            padded["target_places"] = list(block["target_places"])
            padded["parent"] = "exact"
            padded["mix"] = "germany"
            padded["source"] = SOURCE
            padded["cut"] = cut
            out.append(padded)
    return out

def make_blocks(
    triangle: Path,
    out: Path,
    first_date: str,
    truth_delay: int,
    workers: int = 4,
) -> int:
    """Cut the German blocks of `window` and pickle them in cut order."""
    as_of, truth_until = window(first_date, truth_delay)
    counts = german_counts(pd.read_csv(triangle), as_of)
    cuts = cut_dates(FIRST_CUT, truth_until)
    jobs = [(counts, c, i, truth_until) for i, c in enumerate(cuts)]
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(workers) as pool:
        blocks = [b for part in pool.map(_cut, jobs) for b in part]
    with out.open("wb") as f:
        pickle.dump(blocks, f)
    print(
        f"{len(blocks)} blocks of {len(cuts)} cuts {cuts[0]} to {cuts[-1]}, "
        f"reports to {as_of}, truth to {truth_until}: {out}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return len(blocks)

docs.title: How it is used in the workflow
docs.text:
It is the real-data benchmark for the baselines and the fine-tuned model. The nowcastgermany command fetches the hub's data (fetch), runs the benchmark (backtest) and reads the hub teams' forecasts (teams).

In the workflow, germany_triangle fetches the triangle. score_germany and score_run_germany score each fine-tuned checkpoint on it with nowcastgermany.checkpoint. real_training_blocks cuts the German training blocks for the real-data ablation with nowcastgermany.finetune_blocks. publish_germany_unit attaches a checkpoint's German forecasts to its release (nowcastgermany unit-publish).

The paper workflow runs the German study in germany_fetch, germany_development and germany_heldout.

The Site workflow loads the pinned checkpoint's stored forecasts (ft-tag, ft-load), scores the hub teams (teams, asof, paper) and builds the German nowcast benchmark page.
